text:
lia (pm): Quick sync — we need a proposal for the automatic fallback orchestration UX. Focus: how we present degrade modes, error-trigger rules, and the audit trail. Short thread before sprint planning.

alex (eng): Top-level ask — make it obvious which fallback kicked in and why. Users should see: trigger, active fallback variant, and time range.

kevin (infra): +1. Also show the policy TTL and hysteresis so people know when we'll revert. Example policy view mock: ```json
{
  "policy_name": "slow-tier-fallback",
  "triggers": ["5xx_rate>0.05", "p95_latency>1s"],
  "mode": "quota-scaled",
  "ttl_seconds": 300,
  "hysteresis": 60
}
```

maria (devex): UX notes: 1) show a collapsed timeline with the last 24h degradations, 2) an inline explain button that surfaces the exact metric that tripped the policy, 3) ability to simulate a trigger (dry-run) from the policy page.

lia (pm): Who can edit these policies? Need RBAC: read-only for product, edit for platform owners, and audit-only for compliance. Also audit log must be immutable.

kevin (infra): RBAC should map to teams in the console — add a soft-lock when a policy is in canary. E.g., if rollout_active == true then require approver.

alex (eng): For audit we should capture original request context + route selected + model variant + decision trace id. That helps debug quality regressions. Event payload size might be big, so we should sample verbose traces.

lia (pm): Sampling rules: defaults to 1% heavy trace, 10% metadata traces, configurable per-customer. Need a way to flag traces for retention if they correlate with user error budgets.

kevin (infra): Implementation note: store full traces in cold storage (30d) and indexes in hot store (7d) for quick playback. Console should show playback link and reason tag.

maria (devex): UX control: when editing a policy show a preview of affected routes and an estimated cost delta (tokens/sec impact). Add a preview sandbox button that runs the policy against historical traffic for 1h.

lia (pm): Good. Also: what about graceful degradation modes — we have: silent-drop, partial-degrade (compress response), fallback-variant. How to present choices?

alex (eng): Present them as ordered options with risk meter. E.g., "silent-drop (lowest cost, highest user-visible failures)" vs "fallback-variant (higher cost, preserves UX)". Include an automated recommendation engine that selects based on SLA priority.

kevin (infra): Add an "explainability" row: when fallback triggers, show short summary + link to full decision tree and the exact rule that matched.

lia (pm): Ops playbook integration: when policy triggers, optionally open a runbook incident stub with prefilled cause, affected routes, and suggested mitigations. @sachin can you validate operational flow?

sachin (sre): Yup. The stub needs TL;DR, steps to rollback, and contact list. We should also auto-attach recent logs (last 5m) and a link to the playback. Fine to auto-open only for high-severity triggers.

maria (devex): Small nit — policy edit history: show diffs and who approved. Add a "replay" button that re-runs the policy logic against a stored trace for repro.

alex (eng): Edge case: when multiple fallbacks could apply simultaneously, show the precedence and allow manual override. Also surface oscillation detection and auto-extend TTL if we detect flapping.

kevin (infra): For override we need a cooldown and audit entry: who forced it and for how long. Also a button to schedule a safe rollback.

lia (pm): OK action items: (1) kevin + alex: draft policy JSON schema with TTL/hysteresis/precedence + sampling keys. (2) maria: wireframe policy page with timeline + simulate + replay. (3) sachin: runbook stub template and severity thresholds. (4) me: consolidate RBAC and approval flow.

infra-bot: Deploy preview cluster created: https://staging.redwood.test/policies/preview/1765000000 (expires in 72h) :rocket:

maria (devex): I'll start the wireframes and attach to the ticket. Recommend adding an inline "why this matters" tooltip for each degrade mode.

kevin (infra): One more thought — allow a pre-commit dry-run: when someone saves a policy, run it against a 1h sample of traffic and show estimated false-positive rate. That reduces accidental triggers.

lia (pm): Perfect. If there's no objections I'll slot this into sprint planning and include prototype time. Thanks everyone :heart:
